chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the child of al-mula'ana (the cursing/disowning), who would inherit him? He said: 'His mother'. So I said, 'If his mother is dead, who would inherit him?' He said: 'His maternal uncles'.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits a child from al-mula'ana if the mother is deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that in cases of 'al-mula'ana' where paternity is denied, the child's lineage is traced exclusively to the mother, making her the primary heir. If the mother predeceases the child, the inheritance passes to the maternal uncles (akhwal), reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the maternal line determines inheritance rights in the absence of a recognized father. This ruling underscores the significance of the mother's role in preserving the child's identity and property rights within the family structure.
